scientific_findings.construction_policy: Both manuscripts distinguish requested cap from the realized local basis rank. Native initialization is min(cap, ambient dimension, actual local reference count minus one), with the published default cap 20; numerical eigenvalue/range reductions and the rank-one stopping convention are qualified. The risk implementation is not assigned the forecasting wrapper's rank-zero fallback.
scientific_findings.forecast_results: The selected-cap bounded KAHM has 3.26% lower nonlinear aggregate SMSE than the historical cap-two arm; native cap 20 is 8.39% worse. Exactly three of the six prespecified primary margin comparisons are established, so the full criterion remains unmet. The policy comparator has lower aggregate loss than KAHM. The matched-bank decomposition attributes the overall cap-selection loss decrease to the common-component decrease, while the geometric increment becomes less favorable.
scientific_findings.forecast_selection: The main forecast comparison uses the full ten-procedure roster. Independent B-only cap selection precedes C-only calibration/policy selection; test outcomes do not select caps. Independently selected primary controls are distinguished from secondary controls at the KAHM-selected bank. Equal validation roles are not presented as equal search counts or compute.
scientific_findings.historical_scope: Older fixed-cap studies and their numerical assets are retained and explicitly scoped. The forecasting supplement does not present the superseded cap-two principal experiment as the current principal result. The risk two-lag study is correctly described as permitting its full two-dimensional ambient space.
scientific_findings.risk_results: Validation-selected caps improve descriptive mean test MSE in 18 repetitions and tie in eight, with none worse than cap two. The selected KAHM tolerance decisions remain identical across the three policies. All 234 selected KAHM horizon lower endpoints are zero, and none of the 234 policy-switch improvement endpoints is positive. Prefix-improvement certificates are identified as fitted-forecast comparisons, not differences of unknown class-optimal risks.
scientific_findings.risk_selection_and_event: Each risk-policy arm chooses one whole bank and a forecast prefix using independent development data, then retains all four nested prefixes from that bank. The new campaign allocates failure probability across 3,744 risk tails and 936 fitted-improvement tails in 26 repetitions; its 4,680-tail event is not extended to other studies. Episode averages and disjoint episode pairs are the sampling units.
scientific_findings.style_and_provenance: Changed prose presents methods, results and limitations scientifically, without revision-response narrative. The existing journal layouts and author metadata are preserved. Historical public commits are distinguished from the accompanying new research sources; no new unpublished paths are claimed to exist at those historical commits.
scientific_findings.theory: Forecast fixed-geometry span/bounded-correction proofs and risk certificate theory remain intact. The general option to choose among a simultaneously calibrated frozen family is preserved; the new study's earlier cap/history/prefix choices are a specific protocol, not a replacement theorem requirement.
